source_text:
Ποία

σαγήνη χωρῆσαι τὸν «χαρακτῆρα τῆς ὑποστάσεως» δύναται; Τίς ἐπιλαβέσθαι χειρὶ
2
τοῦ «τῷ ῥήματι τῆς οἰκείας δυνάμεως τὰ πάντα φέροντος»; «Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ
διώκεις.» Νυμφαγωγόν σε τῆς ἐμῆς νύμφης τηρῶ. Τί με διώκεις ὑπὲρ οὗ μικρὸν
ὕστερον διώκεσθαι μέλλεις; Ἀλλὰ σκύλλεις εἰκῇ τοὺς πόδας, μάτην ἱδροῖς, περιττῶς
κοπιᾷς· ἐν τοῖς κόλποις τοῦ πατρὸς ὁ παρὰ σοῦ διωκόμενος κάθηται. «Ἐγώ εἰμι
Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις», ἀγνοῶν ὅτι πρὸς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ μάχει ζωήν. Τῷ σοφῷ τί σὺ
πολεμεῖς, τοξεύεις εὐεργέτην οἷον οὐκ ἔχεις ἕτερον, τροφέα λακτίζεις δι' ὃν ἡ γῆ σοι
χωρὶς ὄκνου τῶν καρπῶν ἀνατέλλει τὴν τράπεζαν; Σωτῆρα φαυλίζεις, ὃς ἐὰν σφίγξῃ
τὴν χεῖρα, τίς σε τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ἐλευθεροῖ, τίς ἀπολύει τῶν δεσμῶν, παρὰ τίνι
εὑρήσεις τὸ χειρόγραφον;»
7 Οὕτως οὖν οὗτος ὁ Παῦλος ὅ ποτε διώκτης νῦν εὐαγγελιστής, ὅ ποτε
πειρατὴς νῦν κυβερνήτης, ὅ ποτε λύκος νῦν ποιμήν, ὅ ποτε μόλιβδος νῦν χρυσίον, ὅ
ποτε βλάσφημος νῦν εὐφημῶν καὶ ὑπὸ πάντων εὐφημούμενος, οὗτος ἐν
διδασκάλοις ἔξαρχος, ἐν θεοφόροις ἐξαίρετος, ἐν προφήταις τρανός, ἐν ἀποστόλοις
σοφώτερος, ἐν ἀθληταῖς ἄτρωτος, τῶν τῆς ἀληθείας κηρύκων ἐνδοξότερος, τῶν τῆς
εὐσεβείας στρατιωτῶν δυνατώτερος. Τίς γὰρ «τρὶς ἐρραβδίσθη» καὶ τέταρτον
ηὔχετο; Τίς «πεντάκις τεσσαράκοντα παρὰ μίαν ἔλαβεν ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων», ὡς
ἐκεῖνος σεμνύνεται; Τίς «πεποιηκὼς ἐν τῷ βυθῷ νυχθήμερον» ἀντὶ νυμφικοῦ λουτροῦ προφέρει τὸ ναυάγιον, «ὁδοιπορίαις πολλάκις» ἀλλὰ πάσας ἐπικερδεῖς ἑκάστην
πολυκερδῆ κτισάμενος; Τίς «κινδύνοις λῃστῶν, κινδύνοις ἐκ γένους, κινδύνοις
ποταμῶν, κινδύνοις ἐν ἐρημίᾳ, κινδύνοις ἐξ ἐθνῶν, κινδύνοις ἐν ψευδαδέλφοις»,
καὶ τῆς ὑπομονῆς τὸν πλοῦτον οὐκ ἐσκόρπισεν; Τίς ὅλων τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν περιφέρει
τὴν μέριμναν, τῶν φορτίων δὲ τὴν πεῖραν οὐ στενοῖ οὐδὲ τοὺς ὤμους βαρεῖ οὐδὲ τὰ
νῶτα κάμπτεται; Τίς ἄρα τοσοῦτον μὲν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν βδελύττεται, σπλάγχνα δὲ περὶ
τοὺς ἁμαρτωλοὺς τοιαῦτα κέκτηται; Οὐδείς· πρεσβεύει γὰρ πάντοτε τυχεῖν ἡμᾶς τῶν
αἰωνίων ἀγαθῶν, ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν, ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς
αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.

3
thought_title: Christ's rhetorical questions to Saul and Paul's transformation
orientation: Christ continues speaking to Saul on the road, asking rhetorical questions that show the futility of persecuting him, and then the homilist praises Paul's transformation from persecutor to evangelist.
pass_a_gloss: What net is able to contain the exact imprint of God's being? Who can lay hold with a hand of the one who bears all things by the word of his own power? I am Jesus whom you persecute. I keep you as the bridal escort of my bride. Why do you persecute me, for whom a little later you are about to be persecuted? But you wear out your feet in vain, you sweat to no purpose, you labor superfluously; in the bosom of the Father sits the one persecuted by you. I am Jesus whom you persecute, not knowing that you fight against your own life. Why do you war against the wise one, you shoot arrows at a benefactor such as you have no other, you kick the nourisher through whom the earth without hesitation makes the table of fruits spring up for you? You disparage the Savior, who if he closes his hand, who frees you from your sins, who releases you from your bonds, from whom will you find the certificate of debt? Thus therefore this Paul, the once persecutor now evangelist, the once pirate now pilot, the once wolf now shepherd, the once lead now gold, the once blasphemer now speaking well and being spoken well of by all, this one among teachers is leader, among God-bearers is exceptional, among prophets is clear, among apostles is wiser, among athletes is unwounded, more glorious than the heralds of truth, more powerful than the soldiers of piety. For who was beaten with rods three times and prayed for a fourth? Who five times received forty lashes minus one from the Jews, as that one boasts? Who having spent a night and a day in the deep brings forward the shipwreck instead of a bridal bath, in journeys often but having made all of them profitable, each one much-gaining? Who in dangers from robbers, dangers from his own race, dangers from rivers, dangers in the wilderness, dangers from Gentiles, dangers among false brothers, did not scatter the wealth of his endurance? Who carries the care of all the churches, but does not narrow the experience of the burdens nor weigh down the shoulders nor bend the back? Who therefore so much abhors sin, but possesses such bowels of compassion toward sinners? No one; for he always intercedes that we may obtain the eternal good things, in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom be the glory and the might unto the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: Uses the glossary rendering for this title from Hebrews 1:3.

choices.term: τῷ ῥήματι τῆς οἰκείας δυνάμεως τὰ πάντα φέροντος
choices.english: the one who bears all things by the word of his own power
choices.why: Keeps the participial construction and the phrase 'word of his own power' close to the Greek, echoing Hebrews 1:3.
rejected: the one who upholds all things by his powerful word

choices.term: νυμφαγωγόν σε τῆς ἐμῆς νύμφης τηρῶ
choices.english: I keep you as the bridal escort of my bride
choices.why: Preserves the image of Paul as the one who leads the bride (the Church) to Christ, and the present tense of τηρῶ.
rejected: I am keeping you as the one who escorts my bride

choices.english: you shoot arrows at a benefactor
choices.why: Keeps the specific image of shooting arrows, which the checker flagged as lost in 'assail'.
Renders the specific legal document of Colossians 2:14, not a generic 'bond' which could be confused with fetters.

choices.english: from whom will you find the certificate of debt
choices.why: παρὰ with dative here means 'from whom', not 'with whom', as the checker noted.
rejected: with whom will you find the certificate of debt

pass_b_english: What net can contain “the exact imprint of God’s being” (Hebrews 1:3)? Who can lay a hand on “the one who bears all things by the word of his power” (Hebrews 1:3)? “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.” I keep you as the bridal escort of my bride. Why do you persecute me, the one for whom you will shortly be persecuted? But you wear out your feet in vain, you sweat for nothing, you labor uselessly; the one you are persecuting sits in the Father’s bosom. “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,” not knowing that you are fighting against your own life. Why do you make war on the wise one? You wound a benefactor such as you have no other; you kick the nourisher for whose sake the earth without hesitation makes the table of fruits spring up for you. You despise the Savior, who, if he clenches his hand, who will free you from your sins? Who will release you from your bonds? In whose possession will you find the certificate of debt?”

So then this Paul, once a persecutor, is now an evangelist; once a pirate, now a pilot; once a wolf, now a shepherd; once lead, now gold; once a blasphemer, now speaking well and spoken well of by all. He is a leader among teachers, exceptional among the God-bearing, clear among prophets, wiser among apostles, unwounded among athletes, more glorious than the heralds of truth, more powerful than the soldiers of piety. For who “was beaten with rods three times” and prayed for a fourth? Who “five times received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one” (2 Corinthians 11:24-25), as he boasts? Who, “having spent a night and a day in the deep” (2 Corinthians 11:25), presents the shipwreck instead of a bridal bath, “often in journeys” (2 Corinthians 11:26) but making all of them profitable, each one richly profitable? Who faced “dangers from robbers, dangers from his own people, dangers from rivers, dangers in the wilderness, dangers from the Gentiles, dangers among false brothers” (2 Corinthians 11:26), and did not scatter the wealth of his endurance? Who carries the care of all the churches, yet is not constrained by the experience of burdens, nor are his shoulders weighed down, nor does he bend his back? Who then so detests sin, yet has such compassion for sinners? No one. For he always intercedes that we may obtain eternal good things, in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom be glory and power forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: You shoot arrows at a benefactor such as you have no other
problems.source_quote: τοξεύεις εὐεργέτην οἷον οὐκ ἔχεις ἕτερον
problems.why: "shoot arrows" misreads τοξεύεις; in context it means "wound/harm" metaphorically, not literal archery.
problems.fix: You wound a benefactor such as you have no other

problems.quote: the earth without hesitation makes the table of its fruits spring up for you
problems.source_quote: ἡ γῆ σοι χωρὶς ὄκνου τῶν καρπῶν ἀνατέλλει τὴν τράπεζαν
problems.why: "table of its fruits" garbles syntax; τὴν τράπεζαν is object, τῶν καρπῶν genitive: "makes the table of fruits spring up."
problems.fix: the earth without hesitation makes the table of fruits spring up for you

problems.quote: who, if he closes his hand
problems.why: "closes his hand" misses that σφίγξῃ is "clenches/shuts tight" in judgment, withholding blessing; "closes" too weak.
problems.fix: who, if he clenches his hand

problems.quote: From whom will you find the certificate of debt?
problems.why: "From whom" for παρὰ τίνι is wrong; it means "with/at whose place," i.e., "in whose possession will you find?"
problems.fix: In whose possession will you find the certificate of debt?

problems.quote: does not shrink from the experience of burdens
problems.source_quote: τῶν φορτίων δὲ τὴν πεῖραν οὐ στενοῖ
problems.why: "shrink from" is wrong; στενοῖ means "is cramped/narrowed by," i.e., is not constrained/crushed by.
problems.fix: is not constrained by the experience of burdens

problems.quote: the one who bears all things by the word of his own power
problems.source_quote: τοῦ «τῷ ῥήματι τῆς οἰκείας δυνάμεως τὰ πάντα φέροντος»
problems.why: Source says 'by the word of his power', not 'his own power'; οἰκείας modifies ῥήματι not δυνάμεως.
problems.fix: the one who bears all things by the word of his power
problems.ruling: οἰκείας modifies ῥήματι, not δυνάμεως: 'his own word of power', not 'word of his own power'.

problems.why: Source says 'nor does he bend his back' (middle κάμπτεται), not 'nor bend his back' (imperative/infinitive).
problems.fix: nor does he bend his back
problems.ruling: κάμπτεται is middle indicative 'he bends', not imperative/infinitive 'bend'; English 'nor bend his back' is ungrammatical and changes syntax.

edits.old: You shoot arrows at a benefactor such as you have no other
edits.new: You wound a benefactor such as you have no other

edits.old: the earth without hesitation makes the table of its fruits spring up for you
edits.new: the earth without hesitation makes the table of fruits spring up for you

edits.old: who, if he closes his hand
edits.new: who, if he clenches his hand

edits.old: From whom will you find the certificate of debt?
edits.new: In whose possession will you find the certificate of debt?

edits.old: does not shrink from the experience of burdens
edits.new: is not constrained by the experience of burdens

edits.old: the one who bears all things by the word of his own power
edits.new: the one who bears all things by the word of his power
nor does he bend his back

fixed: τοξεύεις εὐεργέτην: τοξεύεις means 'shoot arrows at', but in context it is metaphorical for wounding/harming; 'wound' is the better rendering.
τῶν καρπῶν ἀνατέλλει τὴν τράπεζαν: 'table of its fruits' misplaces the genitive; 'table of fruits' is correct.
σφίγξῃ τὴν χεῖρα: 'closes' is too weak; 'clenches' better conveys the sense of shutting tight in judgment.
παρὰ τίνι εὑρήσεις: 'From whom' is wrong; παρὰ with dative means 'with/in the possession of'.
τὴν πεῖραν οὐ στενοῖ: 'shrink from' is wrong; στενοῖ means 'is cramped/constrained by'.
τῷ ῥήματι τῆς οἰκείας δυνάμεως: 'his own power' misplaces the adjective; 'his power' is correct.
οὐδὲ τὰ νῶτα κάμπτεται: 'nor bend his back' loses the middle voice; 'nor does he bend his back' is correct.

problems.why: Ungrammatical verb form ('Who ... nor weigh') and wrong agency: his shoulders are not weighed down by the burdens, rather than Paul weighing them down.
problems.fix: nor are his shoulders weighed down
problems.ruling: οὐδὲ τοὺς ὤμους βαρεῖ: burdens should not weigh Paul’s shoulders, not Paul weighing them.

edits.old: nor weigh down his shoulders, nor does he bend his back
edits.new: nor are his shoulders weighed down, nor does he bend his back

fixed: nor weigh down his shoulders: fixed grammar and agency to `nor are his shoulders weighed down` for source οὐδὲ τοὺς ὤμους βαρεῖ.
You wound a benefactor: no edit - wound acceptably renders τοξεύεις without stiff literalism.
table of fruits: no edit - source τῶν καρπῶν has no `its`.
clenches his hand: no edit - correctly renders ὃὰν σφίγξῃ τὴν χεῖρα.
In whose possession: no edit - correctly renders παρὰ τίνι.
is not constrained by the experience of burdens: no edit - correctly renders τῶν φορτίων δὲ τὴν πεῖραν οὐ στενοῖ.
by the word of his power: no edit - `his` already renders τῆς οἰκείας δυνάμεως without stiff `his own`.
nor does he bend his back: no edit - correctly renders οὐδὲ τὰ νῶτα κάμπτεται with parallel grammar.

last_rejected.quote: Who can lay a hand on “the one who bears all things by the word of his power” (Hebrews 1:3)?
last_rejected.source_quote: τοῦ «τῷ ῥήματι τῆς οἰκείας δυνάμεως τὰ πάντα φέροντος»
last_rejected.why: The phrase 'τῷ ῥήματι τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ' is Hebrews 1:3b, not a separate citation; the English splits one Hebrews 1:3 reference into two.
last_rejected.fix: Merge both Hebrews 1:3 references into one, or cite the second as 'Hebrews 1:3' without implying a separate verse.
last_rejected.ruling: Both phrases are from Hebrews 1:3; splitting one verse into two parenthetical citations is a formatting choice, not a meaning error.

last_rejected.quote: I keep you as the bridal escort of my bride
last_rejected.source_quote: Νυμφαγωγόν σε τῆς ἐμῆς νύμφης τηρῶ
last_rejected.why: Christ speaks, but 'I keep you' reverses agency: Christ keeps Saul as escort, not 'I keep you' as recipient.
last_rejected.fix: I keep you as escort of my bride
last_rejected.ruling: σε is accusative object of τηρῶ; 'I keep you' correctly has Christ keeping Saul. No agency reversal.

last_rejected.quote: Why do you persecute me, the one for whom you will shortly be persecuted?
last_rejected.source_quote: Τί με διώκεις ὑπὲρ οὗ μικρὸν ὕστερον διώκεσθαι μέλλεις;
last_rejected.why: ὑπὲρ οὗ = 'for whom' (Christ), but 'the one for whom you will be persecuted' obscures that Paul will suffer for Christ's sake.
last_rejected.fix: Why do you persecute me, for whom you will shortly be persecuted?
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπὲρ οὗ = 'on behalf of whom'; 'for whom you will be persecuted' correctly conveys suffering for Christ's sake.

last_rejected.why: τοξεύεις = 'you shoot (with arrows)', not 'wound'; specific image of archery lost.
last_rejected.ruling: τοξεύεις literally 'shoot with arrows'; 'wound' is within normal range, archery implied but meaning preserved.

last_rejected.quote: the earth without hesitation makes the table of fruits spring up for you
last_rejected.source_quote: ἡ γῆ σοι χωρὶς ὄκνου τῶν καρπῶν ἀνατέλλει τὴν τράπεζαν
last_rejected.why: τὴν τράπεζαν = 'the table' as object, but 'makes the table of fruits spring up' is confused; earth brings forth the table of fruits.
last_rejected.fix: the earth without reluctance brings forth the table of fruits for you
last_rejected.ruling: τὴν τράπεζαν = 'table'; earth ἀνατέλλει τὴν τράπεζαν τῶν καρπῶν = 'makes table of fruits spring up'. Translation conveys this.

last_rejected.quote: who, if he clenches his hand
last_rejected.why: σφίγξῃ τὴν χεῖρα = 'closes his hand' (withholds bounty), not 'clenches' in anger; changes theological image.
last_rejected.fix: who, if he closes his hand
last_rejected.ruling: σφίγξῃ τὴν χεῖρα = 'clench/close hand'; 'clenches' is valid rendering, withholding-bounty sense contextually clear.

last_rejected.quote: presents the shipwreck instead of a bridal bath
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀντὶ νυμφικοῦ λουτροῦ προφέρει τὸ ναυάγιον
last_rejected.why: προφέρει = 'offers/produces', not 'presents'; Paul offers shipwreck in place of bridal bath, a striking paradox flattened.
last_rejected.fix: offers the shipwreck in place of a bridal bath
last_rejected.ruling: προφέρει = 'bring forward/produce/present'; 'presents' is within normal range, paradox preserved.

last_rejected.quote: yet is not constrained by the experience of burdens
last_rejected.source_quote: τῶν φορτίων δὲ τὴν πεῖραν οὐ στενοῖ
last_rejected.why: στενοῖ = 'does not narrow/distress', not 'constrained'; Paul is not distressed/crushed by burdens.
last_rejected.fix: yet is not distressed by the experience of burdens
last_rejected.ruling: στενοῖ = 'is distressed/constrained'; 'constrained' is valid rendering within normal range, meaning preserved.

last_rejected.why: βαρεῖ = 'weighs down' but subject is Paul; 'nor weigh down' lacks subject/auxiliary, grammatically broken.
last_rejected.fix: nor do they weigh down his shoulders
last_rejected.ruling: Parallel with 'is not constrained'; 'nor weigh down' is minor ellipsis, meaning clear. Not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: nor does he bend his back
last_rejected.why: κάμπτεται = middle/passive 'is bent/bows'; 'nor does he bend his back' suggests active, but Greek is passive or middle.
last_rejected.ruling: κάμπτεται middle/passive; 'does he bend his back' acceptable for middle 'bends (his own) back'. Meaning preserved.

last_rejected.quote: I keep you as the bridal escort of my bride
last_rejected.source_quote: Νυμφαγωγόν σε τῆς ἐμῆς νύμφης τηρῶ
last_rejected.why: Christ's words continue without quotation marks or attribution; reader may miss speaker shift from author to Christ.
last_rejected.fix: Add quotation marks: 'I keep you as escort of my bride.'
last_rejected.ruling: Context and 'I am Jesus' quotation make Christ as speaker clear; missing quotation marks are stylistic, not misleading.

last_rejected.source_quote: Τίς «πεντάκις τεσσαράκοντα παρὰ μίαν ἔλαβεν ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων», ὡς ἐκεῖνος σεμνύνεται; Τίς «πεποιηκὼς ἐν τῷ βυθῷ νυχθήμερον»
last_rejected.why: Citation spans 11:24-25 but 'three times beaten with rods' (11:25) precedes and is separate; 'spent night and day in deep' is 11:25, but 'prayed for fourth' is not in text—'fourth' refers to rods, not in citation.
last_rejected.ruling: Citation covers both 11:24 (forty lashes) and 11:25 (night-and-day in deep); 'prayed for fourth' refers to rods (11:25), not in citation range.
